provenance.task: Settle whether the matched-pair A/B gap (same script run, seconds apart) cancels corpus sensitivity the way an earlier round assumed when it used a single-arm instantaneous floor (~0.006) as the denominator for a 'roughly 5x' claim on the model A/B's MRR gap. Sourced from p6-mechanism's study (reported via team-lead), committed here as a dated result file per team-lead instruction -- the raw data previously lived only in this session's scratchpad (p6gap_samples_model.jsonl / p6gap_samples_chunking.jsonl) and eval/README.md's claim that results/*.json backs every published number was false as long as that remained the case.
provenance.attribution: p6-mechanism ran the study; p6-boostfix committed it, per team-lead routing. Not independently re-run by p6-boostfix.
provenance.method: 36 independent samples each for model_ab (potion-base-8M vs potion-retrieval-32M) and chunking_ab (uniform vs per_turn), run via `python -m eval.model_ab` / `python -m eval.chunking_ab` (module invocation required -- a bare script path fails with ModuleNotFoundError on the sibling `eval.provenance` import). main_session_boost read live from search_module.MAIN_SESSION_BOOST (both scripts' own argparse default), never passed as a literal. MAIN_SESSION_BOOST verified computationally immediately before AND after every single run (boost_before/boost_after/boost_clean fields on every raw record below) -- 0 of 72 runs were dirty; one transient 0.01 reading was caught during setup (some other concurrent process in this shared session momentarily wrote a different value to the uncommitted, dirty search.py), never landed inside a counted sample. Each run built fresh, independent temp indexes (no --index-dir reuse), so this measures real, independent corpus-state sampling over wall-clock time, not artifacts of index reuse.

recall_at_10.note: recall@10 identical between arms in 19/36 runs; differs by exactly one query (+0.0278) in the remaining 17.
recall@10 identical between arms in ALL 36/36 runs.

conclusions.model_ab: Gap DIRECTION is robust: 36/36 runs positive (retrieval-32M > base-8M on overall MRR), never flipped -- a real signal. Gap MAGNITUDE is not stable enough to support a multiple-of-floor claim: the gap's own spread (0.0431) exceeds either arm's individual spread (0.0213 / 0.0380), meaning matched-pairing does NOT cancel corpus sensitivity here -- the two models respond differently enough to the same corpus change that the difference is itself more volatile than either measurement alone. The previously published 'roughly 5x' used a single-arm, 3-replicate, back-to-back floor (~0.006) as the denominator; against the gap's OWN measured spread the published gap (~0.0305) is 0.71x -- under 1x, i.e. not distinguishable from corpus sensitivity as a magnitude claim. Recommended wording: keep the direction claim, drop the multiple.
conclusions.chunking_ab: Existing 'no winner, disagrees in sign' conclusion is CORRECT and this data makes it MORE certain, not less: the matched-pair gap crosses zero repeatedly (7 sign changes across 15 distinct corpus states) and its own spread (0.0361) exceeds either arm's spread alone (0.0213 / 0.0208). No document correction needed here.
